project.name: aboocode
project.description: Open-source core engine of an AI coding agent (opencode derivative): agent runtime, sessions, tools, LLM providers, server/API, memory, team multi-agent, scheduler. Scope: packages/aboocode/src excluding CLI/TUI.

nodes.name: agent.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) server bridge, translating between aboocode's internal agent/session runtime and the ACP transport including prompts, tool calls, usage updates, and model selection.
nodes.languageNotes: Large namespace-based module (ACP, Agent) using nested helper functions for ACP message translation and model/variant resolution.

nodes.name: ACP
nodes.summary: Top-level ACP namespace coordinating context limits, usage reporting, and provider/model resolution for the Agent Client Protocol surface.

nodes.name: Agent
nodes.summary: ACP agent implementation handling prompt turns, tool invocation rendering, and streaming responses to ACP clients.

nodes.name: sendUsageUpdate
nodes.summary: Computes token/cost usage from session state and emits a usage update notification to the ACP client.

nodes.name: toToolKind
nodes.summary: Maps internal tool identifiers to the ACP tool-kind taxonomy used for client-side rendering.

nodes.name: defaultModel
nodes.summary: Resolves the default provider and model to use for an ACP session, including opencode provider fallbacks.

nodes.name: session.ts
nodes.summary: Manages the lifecycle and state of ACP sessions, tracking active sessions and their associated context.

nodes.name: ACPSessionManager
nodes.summary: Stores and retrieves ACP session state objects keyed by session id, coordinating session creation and disposal.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Type definitions for ACP session state and configuration objects shared across the ACP module.

nodes.name: agent.ts
nodes.summary: Core agent registry that loads, merges, and resolves agent definitions (built-in and config-defined), exposing lookup, listing, and default-agent selection plus orchestrator prompt construction.
nodes.languageNotes: Namespace module with lazily-initialized state, reload hooks, and Zod-style Info schemas for agent metadata.

nodes.name: Agent
nodes.summary: Agent namespace providing the registry of agent definitions, their schemas, and resolution logic for the runtime.

nodes.name: buildOrchestratorPrompt
nodes.summary: Assembles the system prompt used by the orchestrator agent from configured instructions and context.

nodes.name: reload
nodes.summary: Reloads agent definitions from configuration and markdown sources, refreshing the in-memory registry state.

nodes.name: defaultAgent
nodes.summary: Determines the default visible primary agent to use when none is explicitly specified.

nodes.name: isolation-path.ts
nodes.summary: Path translation helpers for agent isolation, mapping between an isolated agent root and real filesystem paths and enforcing containment.

nodes.name: IsolationPath

nodes.name: isolation.ts

nodes.name: AgentIsolation

nodes.summary: Constructs an isolation context for an agent, configuring allowed directories, blocked tools, and shell permissions.

nodes.name: isToolBlocked
nodes.summary: Determines whether a given tool is blocked under the active agent isolation policy.

nodes.name: fromRole
nodes.summary: Derives an isolation mode/configuration from an agent role designation.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Credential store for provider authentication, persisting OAuth and API key records to disk and exposing get/set/remove/all operations.

nodes.name: Auth
nodes.summary: Auth namespace defining credential schemas (Oauth, Api, WellKnown) and CRUD operations over the on-disk auth store.

nodes.name: install

nodes.name: registry.ts

nodes.name: PackageRegistry

nodes.name: bus-event.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the typed event definition helper used to declare strongly-typed events for the application event bus.

nodes.name: BusEvent
nodes.summary: BusEvent namespace providing the define() factory and Definition type for declaring bus event schemas and payloads.

nodes.name: global.ts

nodes.name: Control

nodes.name: debug-log.ts

nodes.name: DebugLog

nodes.name: index.ts

nodes.name: Env

nodes.name: index.ts

nodes.summary: Detects the host IDE and installs the companion editor extension, surfacing already-installed and install-failure errors.

nodes.name: language.ts
nodes.summary: Static mapping of file extensions to LSP language identifiers used when opening documents.

tour.title: Process Entry & Bootstrap
tour.description: Start where the runtime starts. index.ts is the top-level package entry point: it bootstraps the global filesystem paths (config, data, cache, state) defined in global/index.ts and runs storage migrations before any feature code loads. Reading these two files first answers the newcomer's question "what happens the moment `aboo` runs?" and establishes the global environment every later subsystem depends on.

tour.title: Persistence, Event Bus & Config
tour.description: These three are the foundation everything else is built on. storage/db.ts owns the SQLite connection, migrations, and typed transactions; bus/index.ts is the publish/subscribe event bus that decouples subsystems; config/config.ts loads, validates, merges, and patches aboocode config (it has one of the highest fan-out counts in the codebase). Understand these now because the session loop, server, tools, and providers all read config and emit/consume bus events.
tour.languageLesson: aboocode organizes code into TypeScript namespaces (e.g. `export namespace Config`) rather than classes. Each subsystem exposes a flat namespace of functions and types, which keeps the public surface explicit and tree-shakeable under Bun's bundler.

tour.title: Project Instance & Wiring
tour.description: Building on the config and bus from Step 2, this is how a single working project comes alive. project/instance.ts defines the Instance abstraction and binds it to an async context so any code can reach "the current project" without threading it through every call. project/bootstrap.ts is the assembler — it wires together the bus, commands, file subsystem, tools, providers, and more into a live instance. instance.ts has the third-highest fan-in in the whole codebase, which tells you how central it is.
tour.languageLesson: The Instance uses AsyncLocalStorage-style context binding so the "current project" is ambient. This is a common Node/Bun pattern for request- or task-scoped state that avoids passing a context object through every function signature.

tour.title: HTTP Server & Event Stream
tour.description: With a project instance available, aboocode exposes it. server/server.ts is the central Hono HTTP bootstrap that mounts every route module, generates OpenAPI, runs mDNS discovery, and binds the port — this is what `aboo serve` (headless API mode from the README) starts. server/event.ts defines the server Event type that is serialized to clients over SSE, turning internal bus events into a live stream the TUI and web frontends consume.

tour.title: Sessions: The Conversation Runtime
tour.description: This is the heart of the agent. session/index.ts is the Session namespace defining session schemas, persistence, and creation. session/prompt.ts (the largest session module, and second-highest fan-out in the codebase) drives the full prompt lifecycle: it builds user messages, assembles context, and runs the LLM turn loop. These two files are where a user request becomes an actual agent conversation, so they are the pivot point of the whole tour.

tour.title: The Agent Turn Loop & Compaction
tour.description: Continuing the session story, processor.ts orchestrates a single agent turn: it invokes the LLM, handles failures and retries, and dispatches tool calls. compaction.ts solves the context-window problem — it detects overflow, prunes and micro-compacts the message history so long sessions keep working. The script flagged session/{index,prompt,processor,compaction,message-v2} as one tightly coupled cluster, so study them together as the turn-loop subsystem.

tour.title: Agent Definitions & Modes
tour.description: The README describes two built-in agents — build (full-access) and plan (read-only) — plus a @general subagent. agent/agent.ts is the registry that makes this real: it loads, merges, and resolves agent definitions from both built-ins and user config, selects the default agent, and constructs the orchestrator prompt. This is also where v0.9.x subagent model inheritance lives. The processor from Step 6 consults this registry to know which model, tools, and permissions a turn may use.

tour.title: Provider & LLM Integration
tour.description: An agent turn ultimately calls a model, and this layer is how. provider/provider.ts is the registry and SDK factory that resolves providers and models from config and handles auth. provider/transform.ts normalizes messages, prompt caching, and reasoning/thinking options across heterogeneous provider SDKs, while provider/models.ts is the models.dev catalog client that fetches and caches model metadata. Together they let the session loop from Step 5 stay provider-agnostic.
tour.languageLesson: The transform layer adapts one internal message format to many provider-specific shapes — an adapter pattern. Provider caching and reasoning options are negotiated here so the rest of the codebase never branches on which LLM vendor is in use.

tour.title: The Tool System
tour.description: Tools are how the agent acts on the world. tool/tool.ts defines the core Tool abstraction — the namespace, execution Context, and Info shape — and has the second-highest fan-in in the codebase because every concrete tool conforms to it. tool/registry.ts (the single highest fan-out file) aggregates all built-in tools plus plugin- and MCP-provided tools and decides which are available to a given agent. This is the contract that connects the turn loop from Step 6 to real capabilities.

tour.title: Tools in Action: Edit & Delegation
tour.description: Now see the abstraction from Step 9 instantiated. tool/edit.ts implements in-place file modification using a cascading suite of string-replacement strategies — a representative file-mutating tool. tool/task.ts is the TaskTool that spawns sub-agent sessions to perform delegated work, recursively reusing the session machinery from Step 5. These two illustrate the two faces of the toolset: changing the codebase and orchestrating more agents.

tour.title: Permission & Governance
tour.description: Powerful tools need guardrails. permission/index.ts is the permission namespace that tracks pending requests and asks the user (or auto-decides) before a tool runs — this is what enforces the build-vs-plan access difference from Step 7. The hook lifecycle in hook/lifecycle/registry.ts dispatches lifecycle events to registered handlers, and hook/quality-gate.ts implements stop-gate logic that blocks a task from finishing until required verification passes. This is the governance layer that wraps every tool execution.

tour.title: Per-Agent Memory
tour.description: A recent v0.9.x feature: long-term memory. memory/memdir/memdir.ts is the core of the memory-directory subsystem — it builds the memory prompt context and truncates entries to fit the window, feeding remembered knowledge back into the prompt assembly from Step 5. memory/memdir/index.ts is the barrel exposing the subsystem's public surface (scanning, storage, prompts). The script identified the memdir files as a self-contained cluster, so they make a clean single stop.

tour.title: Team & Multi-Agent Coordination
tour.description: Beyond a single delegated task (Step 10), aboocode can run a coordinated team. team/manager.ts orchestrates teams — starting and disbanding them, adding agents, and routing work; team/mailbox.ts is the file-based inter-agent mailbox for sending and reading messages between teammates (the v0.9.x team mailbox). tool/team.ts is the toolset that exposes all of this to an agent, including the batch delegation and circuit-breaker behavior the README mentions.

tour.title: The Scheduler
tour.description: scheduler/index.ts provides a per-instance Scheduler that registers and runs interval- and cron-based work, the foundation of the v0.9.x scheduling subsystem. It lets aboocode wake up and act without a live user turn — for example running recurring maintenance or follow-up tasks — by driving the same session machinery you learned in Step 5 on a timer.
tour.languageLesson: Cron-driven background work in a long-lived process needs careful lifecycle handling: timers must be registered against the project Instance from Step 3 so they are torn down when the instance is disposed, avoiding leaked intervals across hot reloads.

tour.title: External Integrations: MCP & LSP
tour.description: Finally, how aboocode reaches outside itself. mcp/index.ts connects to configured Model Context Protocol servers and surfaces their tools, prompts, and resources into the registry from Step 9 — this is how third-party capabilities plug in. lsp/index.ts spawns per-root Language Server Protocol clients on demand to give the agent hover, definitions, and diagnostics. These integrations close the loop: external tools and language intelligence flow back into the very same session, tool, and permission systems this tour walked through.
tour.languageLesson: Both MCP and LSP are JSON-RPC protocols over a spawned subprocess or socket. aboocode lazily starts a client per server/root and adapts the protocol's tools and capabilities into its own internal abstractions, so external providers look identical to built-in ones to the rest of the engine.
